facts.statement: Dakotasuchus is a genus of mesoeucrocodylian belonging to the family Goniopholididae.
facts.quote: Dakotasuchus (meaning "Dakota [Sandstone] crocodile") is a genus of goniopholidid mesoeucrocodylian.

facts.statement: Fossils of Dakotasuchus were found in the Cenomanian-age Upper Cretaceous Dakota Sandstone in Kansas.
facts.quote: Its fossils have been recovered from the Cenomanian-age Upper Cretaceous Dakota Sandstone of Kansas.

facts.statement: The type specimen was discovered in an iron-cemented sandstone concretion near Salina.
facts.quote: The type specimen was found in an iron-cemented sandstone concretion near Salina.

facts.statement: The animal had twenty pairs of bony scutes running down the midline of its back.
facts.quote: Twenty pairs of bony scutes ran down the midline of the back.

facts.statement: Its short, broad shoulder blades suggest it possessed stout, powerful forelimbs and may have had terrestrial habits.
facts.quote: Dakotasuchus had short broad shoulder blades, suggesting it had stout powerful forelimbs and perhaps terrestrial habits.

facts.statement: M. G. Mehl estimated the complete length of the type individual to be between 3 and 4 meters.
facts.quote: M. G. Mehl, who described the genus, estimated the length of the type individual when complete to have been 3 - 4 m.

facts.statement: The type species, D. kingi, was named in honor of Professor King, a former dean of Kansas Wesleyan University.
facts.quote: The type species is D. kingi, named for Professor King, a former dean of Kansas Wesleyan University.

facts.statement: Robert Carroll assigned Dakotasuchus to the family Goniopholididae in 1988.
facts.quote: Robert Carroll assigned Dakotasuchus to Goniopholididae in 1988.

facts.statement: In 2017, additional fossils including a coracoid, scutes, a dorsal vertebra, and postcranial bones were found in the Mussentuchit Member of the Cedar Mountain Formation in Utah.
facts.quote: In 2017, fossils of Dakotasuchus kingi which consisted of a coracoid, scutes, a dorsal vertebrate and postcranial bones were found in Utah, specifically in the Cedar Mountain Formation's Mussentuchit Member.

facts.statement: The Paleobiology Database lists Pholidosauridae as the parent group for Dakotasuchus.
Dakotasuchus is classified within the family Pholidosauridae.
Dakotasuchus lived from the Albian to the Cenomanian stages, between 106.3 and 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Albian to Cenomanian (106.3 to 93.9 million years ago)
